summary_html: Family agrees to a **voluntary service plan**—counseling, substance-use treatment, parenting classes—designed to correct conditions without court compulsion. Federal law prioritizes family preservation through prevention and support services.

case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.case_name: JET v. State, Department of Family Services
key_cases.holding: The Court affirmed the refusal to let a young mother withdraw her admission of neglect, holding the juvenile court gave the statutorily required advisements at the initial hearing and did not abuse its discretion despite her claim of mental illness and her own earlier requests for help.
key_cases.relevance: Shows the limits of the argument that voluntary help-seeking should insulate a family from formal court action.
key_cases.quote: The juvenile court did not abuse its discretion in denying the appellant's motion to withdraw her admission of neglect

key_cases.court: United States Court of Appeals for the Tenth Circuit
key_cases.holding: The Tenth Circuit affirmed the denial of qualified immunity to caseworkers who removed a chronically ill child from his home without a warrant or pre-deprivation hearing, holding their failure to offer reasonably available preventive services that would have eliminated the need for removal was objectively unreasonable.
key_cases.relevance: Establishes that voluntary and preventive services are not optional courtesies when they would obviate removal.
key_cases.quote: In light of these circumstances, Defendants' failure to provide the Roskas with preventive services to eliminate the need for removal was not reasonable

key_cases.case_name: Matter of Termination of Parental Rights to ALRW
key_cases.holding: The Court affirmed termination under Wyo. Stat. Ann. § 14-2-309(a)(iii), holding that the sufficiency of the Department's reasonable efforts is assessed case by case and that the Department must tie its efforts to the reasons that necessitated the child's out-of-home placement.
key_cases.relevance: Voluntary engagement in services is measured against the conditions that caused the removal.
key_cases.quote: We assess whether sufficient evidence supports that DFS made reasonable efforts to rehabilitate the family on a case-by-case basis

state_agency.name: Wyoming Department of Family Services
state_agency.hotline: No statewide hotline. Call the DFS field office in the county where the child lives — the list is at dfs.wyo.gov/about/contact-us

common_failures: Failure to consider less restrictive alternatives

timeline_requirements.deadline: 48 hours, excluding weekends and legal holidays
timeline_requirements.starts_from: Child taken into temporary protective custody
timeline_requirements.consequence_of_miss: Not specified in statute; full-time shelter care continues only if the court finds at the hearing that it is required (Wyo. Stat. § 14-3-409(a), (d))

parent_rights_at_moment: Right to know where child is going
Right to a shelter care hearing as soon as reasonably possible and no later than 48 hours, excluding weekends and legal holidays (Wyo. Stat. § 14-3-409(a))
A DFS caseworker cannot take your child: only a law enforcement officer, a treating physician, physician's assistant or nurse practitioner, or a court order can (Wyo. Stat. § 14-3-405)
what_to_say: Do you have a court order for removal?
What is the specific imminent danger?
Where are you taking my child?
